collection.description: One serial, operator-invoked run of `mrf-honest scorecard --profile csv` per target under the default retrieval policy: identified User-Agent with a contact address, HTTPS only, robots.txt fetched and obeyed in code before every request, conditional revalidation against the verified cache, retry backoff, and the default 1 GiB decoded-size ceiling. The policy is byte-identical to the one 2026-08-19 was collected under, which is what makes the two cohorts comparable. Every target's URL was re-resolved from its own origin's `cms-hpt.txt`, retrieved the same day; twenty-four of the twenty-five are published today at the same URL, byte for byte, as on 2026-08-19. The exception is Whitfield Medical Surgical Hospital: msh.ms.gov's robots.txt answered HTTP 301 on 2026-09-12, so under RFC 9309 2.3.1.4 this tool could not retrieve that origin's cms-hpt.txt at all and the origin no longer declares the file. The file itself is still served at the URL the 2026-08-19 TXT published, which is the URL this row was retrieved from, and that discrepancy is stated here rather than hidden behind an unchanged grade. Of the twenty-five attempts, 13 revalidated against the verified cache and returned HTTP 304, 7 transferred a body, 2 were refused by robots.txt, 2 exceeded this project's own size ceiling, and 1 answered HTTP 404.

sampling_frame.format_rule: A target is graded only where the publication is a CMS hospital CSV document (Tall or Wide). Format was read from the publication during the sibling cohort's review, never from a failed request: the URL's file extension decides where it has one; where it has none, a specific declared media type decides; where the declaration is generic, the retrieved document decides. A ZIP archive is a container, not a CSV file, and grading one against this profile would measure the wrong thing; the 7 ZIP publications remain recorded exclusions of the sibling cohort. A .csv publication whose retrieval failed stays in this cohort and is graded F with the dated reason.
sampling_frame.summary: One stratum, a complete enumeration: every facility of the committed 2026-08-19 seeded random draw (48 facilities from CMS's enumeration of 3024 acute-care, non-federal, 50-states-and-DC hospitals) whose cms-hpt.txt publication the sibling JSON cohort recorded as a CSV-retrievable format_outside_profile exclusion - 25 of the 32 format exclusions; the other 7 are ZIP archives and remain excluded there. Every target is a row in this cohort, graded or stated. Totals describe this cohort, not hospitals as a class, and must never be pooled with the JSON cohort. This cohort re-measures those same 25 targets on 2026-09-12; nothing was re-drawn and no target was added or dropped.

discovery.method: Targets are the sibling cohort's CSV-retrievable format_outside_profile exclusions. For each, the MRF URL is the one the facility's own retrieved cms-hpt.txt published for the matching location entry in the local discovery registry; no URL was hand-assembled. publisher_id is the registrable label of the cms-hpt.txt origin; location_id is the facility name the sibling exclusion recorded, slugged. Each target below records how its location entry was matched. Re-checked on 2026-09-12: every origin's cms-hpt.txt was retrieved again that day and 24 of the 25 still publish the same URL for the same location entry. The 25th, msh.ms.gov, could not be retrieved at all (its robots.txt answered HTTP 301, which RFC 9309 2.3.1.4 makes a complete disallow), so that origin no longer declares the file this cohort grades.

policy: A cohort manifest attests the collection context that assessment rows cannot carry by themselves (docs/PHASE-3-FINDINGS.md). `build_comparison` refuses to compare rows without the operator_controlled_single_run attestation. This cohort grades, under the CMS hospital CSV v3 profile, the facilities the sibling hospital-json-v3-2026-09-12 cohort recorded as format_outside_profile exclusions with a CSV-retrievable publication: nothing was re-drawn and nothing was added, so the two cohorts together account for every facility of the one committed sampling frame. Failures stay in the cohort as rows: a robots.txt disallow and this project's own size ceiling are NOT_GRADED with the reason, and a failed download is an F with the dated reason. The two cohorts must never be pooled into one distribution (docs/how-we-compare.md). Contact evidence stays in the local discovery registry and is never published. This cohort is a re-measurement, not a new draw: its subjects are exactly the subjects of the 2026-08-19 cohort of the same profile, re-retrieved and re-graded on 2026-09-12 under the same retrieval and assessment policies, so the two are comparable row for row with `mrf-honest diff`. The sampling frame below is the committed 2026-08-19 draw and is named rather than re-run; nothing was added, removed, or re-drawn.

statistics.basis: the disposition of every facility in this cohort's probability stratum: each published row of that stratum, and each recorded exclusion, as a share of the sample the frame recorded. Shares describe the drawn sample; they are not weighted by bed count, discharge volume, or spend, and they are never pooled across strata or across cohorts.

refusal.reason: this cohort accounts for only part of its stratum, so a proportion computed here would have a denominator the frame does not recognize
